draft.title: Impacts of manufacturing in Asia
card: Many factories in Asia make goods for export, such as clothes, phones and furniture. Countries such as China and Vietnam have many of them.
Factories create jobs, often for people who moved from farms. Wages can be higher than in farming, and cities near factories grow as workers and services arrive.
Factories can pollute air and water. Some workplaces have long hours, low pay or unsafe conditions.
The same factory can bring both benefits and costs to a place. The mix differs from place to place and workplace to workplace.
draft.remember: Export factories can bring jobs, incomes and city growth, and can also bring pollution and poor conditions.

a.q: Which is a likely benefit of a new export factory zone near a Vietnamese city?
opts: More paid jobs for people from nearby farming areas
Cleaner rivers from the factories' waste
Fewer people moving to the city
Lower pollution from the extra trucks
a.why: Factories create jobs, and many workers come from farming areas. Cleaner rivers is wrong because factories can pollute water, which is a cost.
a.clue: Think about what workers gain, not what the land loses.

b.q: A town in southern China gains a large electronics factory. Workers earn more than on farms, but some work long hours in unsafe rooms. Which statement best describes the impact?
opts: It brings both benefits and costs to the town
It brings benefits only, because incomes rose
It brings costs only, because conditions are unsafe
It brings neither, because the goods are exported
b.why: Higher incomes are a benefit, and long hours and unsafe rooms are a cost. Benefits only is wrong because it ignores the poor conditions that the town also faces.
b.clue: Look for what the scenario says on each side.

a.best: More paid jobs for people from nearby farming areas

b.best: It brings both benefits and costs to the town

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with precise detail ('paid jobs for people from nearby farming areas'). The three distractors are short and plainly implausible, so a student could pick the answer without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Think about what workers gain, not what the land loses' points straight to the only option about workers and rules out the environmental options, which gives the answer away.

a.q: A new export factory zone opens near a city in Vietnam. Which change is a cost rather than a benefit?
opts: Smoke from the zone dirties the air in nearby suburbs
New shops and services open to serve the workers
Former farm workers find paid jobs in the factories
Workers earn more in the zone than they did on farms
